summary: A teacher's first-person account of the school garden at Lincoln Elementary, an urban school, started in September 2023. The garden supports math, science and art learning, environmental awareness, nutrition education and inclusion for students with special needs or English as a second language. It has also built community ties through a 'garden to table' event and volunteers, and it has plans to expand.
one_line: Lincoln Elementary's urban school garden, begun in September 2023, boosts interdisciplinary learning, environmental stewardship, nutrition and community engagement.
key_facts: Lincoln Elementary's school garden was established in September 2023 on a patch of the schoolyard, by a teacher with over a decade of experience.
By October 2023 students were learning math by measuring plant growth, science by observing ecological interconnections, and art by capturing the garden's beauty.
The garden supports inclusion: students with special needs or those learning English as a second language find common ground in shared tasks, using non-verbal communication.
In November 2023 the fourth-grade class found a ladybug colony in a sunflower, prompting discussions of beneficial insects, biodiversity, pollinators and crop rotation.
Student-led projects include a composting program and a 'No Waste Wednesday' initiative.
In spring the garden began supplying fresh produce to the school cafeteria and pupils' plates.
School nutritionist Sarah Martin guided students through the nutritional benefits of the plants they grew; by April 2024 the garden was a living educational tool.
Lincoln Elementary is a modest school in an urban landscape, showing gardens are not limited to rural areas.
Jamal, a once disinterested student, developed a newfound passion for nature and science through the garden.
Local restaurateur James Henderson proposed a 'garden to table' event in May 2024, where students prepared and served dishes from their produce and raised funds for garden maintenance.
Environmental science majors from nearby colleges volunteer at the garden, and it collaborates with local environmental groups and universities.
Former students have started recycling programs at the middle school level, parents report more organic produce and less household food waste, and a community garden sprouted next to the school.
Plans for the next academic year include extending the garden for greater crop variety and adding technology such as weather tracking systems.
